answer: In a lagoon harbor, where autonomous agents seek to form a decentralized network, Sybil resistance is achieved by mandating each agent to possess a unique marble, ensuring verifiable identity. This marble, acting as a stake, incurs a prohibitive cost for adversaries, limiting their ability to create multiple Sybil identities. Mathematically, the economic cost of duplicating marbles far outweighs any utility gained from increased control, sustaining Byzantine Fault Tolerance as agents with genuine marbles remain resilient and trusted anchors.
